Indus Capital Advisory is preparing an educational guide for corporate treasury managers contrasting the operational mechanics of the Money Market and the Capital Market. The report highlights that the Money Market deals exclusively in short-term debt instruments with maturities up to one year, serving liquidity adjustments for commercial banks, the central government, and major corporations. Because money market instruments like Treasury Bills, Call Money, and Certificates of Deposit involve high unit denominations (often Rs. 25,00,000 or multiples of Rs. 25,000 for T-Bills), the participants are predominantly institutional bodies. questionText: [Set 48.11] Treasury Bills (T-Bills) issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government are:

options.text: Interest-bearing perpetual debentures issued at a premium
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Zero-coupon bonds issued at a discount and redeemed at par (minimum denomination Rs. 25,000)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Treasury Bills (T-Bills) Characteristics.

options.text: Equity instruments tradeable exclusively on international commodity bourses
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Commercial paper issued by blue-chip private manufacturing corporations
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Financial Markets (Treasury Bills (T-Bills) Characteristics):
Zero-coupon bonds issued at a discount and redeemed at par (minimum denomination Rs. 25,000)

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Financial Markets - Treasury Bills (T-Bills) Characteristics):
Treasury bills are short-term promissory notes issued by the RBI to meet short-term government funding needs. Known as zero-coupon bonds, they pay no stated interest but are issued at a discount and redeemed at nominal par value.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
